summary: In this excerpt from a fiction narrative, two children, Emma Jane and Rebecca, go door to door selling soap samples. Emma Jane struggles to persuade housewives, while Rebecca unexpectedly succeeds with little effort. The excerpt ends with Rebecca approaching a house where a city-looking man is husking corn on the porch and playfully answers her soap pitch.
one_line: Two children sell soap door to door, and Rebecca unexpectedly finds more success than Emma Jane before meeting a whimsical stranger on a porch.
key_facts: Emma Jane and Rebecca sold soap samples door to door, with one holding the horse while the other approached the house.
The two children agreed they could not approach the subject seriously together, so they parted at the gate of each house.
By this point Emma Jane had disposed of three single cakes of soap.
By this point Rebecca had disposed of three small boxes of soap.
Housewives looked at Emma Jane and desired no soap, even after hearing her description of its merits.
Rebecca achieved results with almost no effort because her customers remembered a present need for soap or reminded themselves they would need it later.
A lady at an upstairs window told Emma Jane, "Go away, little girl; whatever you have in your box we don't want any."
Emma Jane said she had not got over trembling from the last place.
Emma Jane told Rebecca to skip a house with shut blinds in front and set far from the road, and to take the next house instead if nobody was home.
Rebecca walked up the lane to the side door of the house.
On the porch, a good-looking young man sat in a rocking-chair husking corn, and Rebecca could not tell whether he was young or middle aged.
The man had a well-shaven face, a well-trimmed mustache, well-fitting clothes, and an air of the city.
The man introduced himself with a whimsical smile as "the lady of the house at present."
When Rebecca asked whether he needed soap, he replied, "Do I look as if I did?"
